claim: The GS101 hardware candidate preserves the installed touch-controller firmware during probe and exposes touch input without the vendor maintenance interfaces.
oracle: Automatic firmware update is disabled, the two high-level flash entry points return ERROR_OP_NOT_ALLOW, maintenance node registration is excluded, and the actual driver compiles against the new kernel. Physical touch remains a separate acceptance gate.

user_journey.scenario: The phone starts a new kernel after a failed diagnostic boot and the user expects the existing touch firmware and recovery path to remain intact.
user_journey.expected: The driver initializes sensing using the existing controller firmware; it does not auto-upgrade or expose raw maintenance nodes during this bring-up.

invariants: Input scan and interrupt functions remain unchanged
No running build source is modified mid-build
gitnexus: No GitNexus tool available; inspected fts_probe, fts_init_sensing, flashProcedure and flash_burn directly.
ast: Compile extracted real flash function bodies with the new constant guard and no hardware stubs; any active hardware reference fails compilation.

unit.red: Pinned fts.h defines FTS_FW_UPDATE and FW_UPDATE_ON_PROBE; fts_probe invokes the updater and registers maintenance interfaces.
unit.green: Actual flash function refusal, unchanged sensing bodies, maintenance-registration guards and wrong-source rejection passed locally and on Linux.

boundaries: source patch -> actual kernel driver compilation -> staged module load -> evdev -> desktop
